title: Brazil 10-Year Yield Cuts Gains to Hover Around 15.19%
body: Brazil's 10-year government bond yield pared earlier gains to trade around 15.19% in November, after President Lula sought to calm markets with renewed assurances on fiscal adjustment. Lula reiterated that his administration remains committed to fiscal responsibility while also prioritizing social programs, amid mounting pressure to unveil concrete adjustment measures and following a late-October election victory that triggered a sell-off in Brazilian assets. Investors continue to focus on fiscal policy, particularly the government's resolve to contain expenditures and stabilize public debt, which has risen markedly in recent years. At the same time, US nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000 in the latest reading, surpassing all forecasts, while the unemployment rate edged lower. The stronger labor data bolstered expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain a restrictive policy stance for longer. Persistently high interest rates in advanced economies may, in turn, constrain the Brazilian central bank, pressuring it to keep domestic monetary policy tight. title: Oil Rebounds as Middle East Tensions Persist
body: Crude oil climbed back to around $91 a barrel on Friday, reversing earlier losses as markets balanced the risk of renewed US–Iran military tensions against the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough. Investors are now considering whether the conclusion of the US midterm elections could clear the way for fresh action against Iran, potentially jeopardizing oil supplies from the Middle East. The geopolitical backdrop remains tense. Iran reported attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, while data from the UKMTO indicated that incidents involving vessels are continuing at close to record levels. At the same time, there were tentative signs of progress on the diplomatic front, with reports that Iran has sent a new nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar. However, major obstacles persist regarding Iran's nuclear programme. Washington is insisting that Tehran relinquish its nuclear capabilities, while Iran is demanding the lifting of the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and the unfreezing of assets as conditions for fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Despite Friday's rebound, crude oil prices were still down nearly 12% for the week. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Argentina Manufacturing Posts Third Straight Monthly Decline
body: Argentina's manufacturing output fell 1.8% year-on-year in September 2026, a smaller drop than the 3.2% decline recorded in August but still the third consecutive monthly contraction. Ten of the 16 industrial divisions surveyed registered decreases. The steepest declines were in machinery and equipment (-26.8%), other equipment, apparatus and instruments (-22%), and wearing apparel, leather and footwear (-5.3%). Further falls were seen in motor vehicles, bodies, trailers and auto parts (-3.5%); furniture, mattresses and other manufacturing industries (-4.9%); fabricated metal products (-4.0%); and basic metals (-1.1%). Output also contracted in petroleum refining, coke and nuclear fuel (-0.8%), food and beverages (-0.1%), and tobacco products (-6.5%). Over the first nine months of the year, cumulative output was 2.6% lower than in the same period of 2025. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: US Stock Indices Gain as Tech Sector Recovers
body: The S&P 500 climbed more than 0.5% on Friday and the Nasdaq advanced over 1.5%, while the Dow ended roughly unchanged. The rebound came after a sharp sell-off in the prior session—the worst single-day loss since April 2025—which had pushed the Nasdaq into correction territory. The previous decline was driven by worries that Democratic gains in the midterm elections could usher in stricter regulation of the AI industry and dampen investment in the sector. Those concerns sparked heavy selling in technology and AI-related shares and fueled a broader risk-off tone across markets. On Friday, however, a strong comeback in chipmakers helped stabilize sentiment as dip buyers stepped in, powering a sharp recovery in technology stocks. Nvidia rose more than 3%, Micron gained 5%, AMD surged nearly 10%, Tesla advanced over 4.5%, and Lam Research jumped 8%. Among the major hyperscalers, Alphabet added more than 1% and Meta gained over 2%. Economic data also drew attention, with nonfarm payrolls beating expectations and the unemployment rate ticking lower. For the week, the S&P 500 is down nearly 3%, the Dow is off more than 1%, and the Nasdaq is lower by around 5%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Brazil Trade Surplus Hits Six-Month High
body: Brazil's trade surplus jumped 39.4% year-on-year to $9.32 billion in October 2026, beating market expectations of $9 billion and marking a six-month high. Exports advanced 20% to $37.81 billion. Agricultural shipments increased 12.8%, driven by surging exports of live animals (212.1%), rye, oats and other unmilled cereals (12,208.8%), and soybeans (8.9%). Exports from the extractive sector climbed 53.5%, supported by sharp gains in nickel ores (103.1%), precious-metal ores (900.6%), and crude petroleum oils (122.6%). Manufacturing exports rose 7.7%, underpinned by higher sales of soybean meal and other animal feed (39.1%), pulp (25.8%), and fuel oils (164.5%). On the import side, total purchases grew 14.8% to $28.49 billion. Agricultural imports increased 10.1%, extractive-industry imports surged 51.4%, and manufacturing imports expanded 13.1%.
